stops.name: Küsnacht, 6 June 1961: the lightning splits the poplar
stops.campa: At Seestrasse 228, in the house under the sentence of the ever-present god, Carl Gustav Jung dies quietly in the late afternoon of 6 June, his family about him. As he goes, a storm breaks over the lake, and lightning strikes the tall poplar in the garden, the tree he sat beneath, splitting its trunk and strewing the lawn with bark; the household keeps the event as canon. Far off at sea, van der Post, homeward from Africa, sees him on a white mountain, waving. The falls at Laufen keep roaring. The journey from parsonage to parsonage-of-his-own is complete: called and not called, the god was present.
stops.quote_source: Jung's words in Laurens van der Post's vision at sea at the hour of death; van der Post, Jung and the Story of Our Time
